summary: Updates IANA registry rules for the Telephony Routing over IP (TRIP) protocol so postal addresses no longer have to be included in contact information. It updates RFC 3219 and is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: A small paperwork change: people registering something no longer must write down a mailing address.

subtitle: IANA no longer collects postal addresses for TRIP registry entries, for a privacy benefit.

tldr.problem: TRIP registry rules required postal addresses in contact information, although no use for them was identified.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8602 updates RFC 3219 so the IETF no longer requires IANA to collect postal addresses, and IANA removed those already collected.
tldr.outcome: Omitting the addresses gives a privacy benefit, and the RFC identifies no security impact.

today: RFC 8602 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3219. No later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 8602 updates the IANA registry rules for the Telephony Routing over IP (TRIP) protocol. It stops requiring that postal addresses be included in contact information.

The reason given is short: no use for the addresses is identified, and leaving them out provides a privacy benefit. The memo updates RFC 3219.
sections.plainLanguage: If nobody uses the home addresses, it is safer not to keep them.

sections.title: What Changes in the Registries
sections.content:
The update applies to the registration rules for TRIP Attributes (RFC 3219, Section 13.2) and TRIP IP Telephony Administrative Domain (ITAD) Numbers (Section 13.5), following RFC 8126.

The IETF no longer requires IANA to collect postal address information when adding TRIP registry entries. IANA has also removed previously collected postal addresses from the registries.
sections.plainLanguage: The two lists stop asking for addresses, and the addresses already on them were wiped.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
No security impacts of this change have been identified.

The only stated benefit is for privacy, since less personal contact data is kept in the registries.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing gets riskier, and people's addresses are better protected.

references.text: Rosenberg, J., Salama, H., and M. Squire, "Telephony Routing over IP (TRIP)", RFC 3219, January 2002.
Cotton, M., Leiba, B., and T. Narten, "Guidelines for Writing an IANA Considerations Section in RFCs", BCP 26, RFC 8126, June 2017.
